title_o: Thinking about God increases acceptance of artificial intelligence in decision-making

replications.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replications.quote: Fig. 1 shows that our replications produced weaker results than those reported in the original studies. In our replications, the effect of God salience on AI reliance is not statistically different from zero (Studies 1, 2a, 2b, 3, and 5 produced effect sizes, measured by r, of 0.03, 0.02, 0.03, 0.002, and 0.01, respectively—in contrast to the original effect sizes reported for each of the respective studies of 0.19, 0.15, 0.14, 0.11, and 0.19). Fig. 1 omits a conceptual replication of Study 1 that produced a nonsignificant effect in the opposite direction of the original Study 1, t(279) = −1.78, P = 0.077, r = −0.10.....Although the majority of our replications produced results directionally consistent with those of Karataş and Cutright, our results imply that if the effect exists, it is so small that the original studies lacked the power to detect it. || In our replications, the effect of God salience on AI reliance is not statistically different from zero (Studies 1, 2a, 2b, 3, and 5 produced effect sizes, measured by r, of 0.03, 0.02, 0.03, 0.002, and 0.01, respectively—in contrast to the original effect sizes reported for each of the respective studies of 0.19, 0.15, 0.14, 0.11, and 0.19).
